sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si bien* "although it is true that" from B2 Unit 8. It is formal, it takes the indicative, and it grants a fact before you say what matters more. The story of the Afro-Antillean workers is full of this contrast: their work was essential, *si bien* they were paid less.

sections.title: Si bien at work
rows: Si bien su trabajo era esencial, cobraban menos.
Although their work was essential, they were paid less.
Si bien muchos hablaban inglés, se quedaron en Panamá.
Although many spoke English, they stayed in Panama.
Los trabajadores, si bien eran necesarios, vivían separados.
The workers, although they were necessary, lived separately. (*si bien* can sit between commas.)
Su trabajo era esencial; no obstante, cobraban menos.
Their work was essential; nevertheless they were paid less. (*no obstante*, B1 Unit 1.)

items.spanish: Si bien llegaron para trabajar, muchos antillanos se quedaron en Panamá.
items.english: Although they came to work, many West Indians stayed in Panama.

items.spanish: Si bien la obra terminó en 1914, las comunidades antillanas siguieron creciendo.
items.english: Although the work ended in 1914, the Antillean communities kept growing.

items.spanish: Esa música, si bien nació en Panamá, tiene raíces antillanas.
items.english: That music, although it was born in Panama, has Antillean roots.

items.spanish: Si bien la Constitución de 1941 cambió la regla, la de 1946 la corrigió.
items.english: Although the Constitution of 1941 changed the rule, the one of 1946 corrected it.

sections.content: After *si bien* use the indicative, because you are confirming a fact; do not add *que* and do not add *pero* in the main clause. It is two words with no accent: *sí* with an accent means "yes". For "even if" (a possibility) you still need *aunque* with the subjunctive.
